title: Nintedanib · continuation
purpose: To continue controlling lung cancer after combination treatment, while benefit continues and side effects remain acceptable.

agents.name: Nintedanib
agents.mechanism: Blocks VEGF, FGF and PDGF receptor signalling
agents.explanation: Nintedanib blocks several signals involved in the growth of blood vessels that support a tumour. Its effects can also cause diarrhoea, liver changes, bleeding and wound-healing problems.
visual: Blocks VEGF, FGF and PDGF receptor signalling
Healthy tissues may also be affected
agents.watch: Call early for diarrhoea or poor fluid intake; report bleeding, yellow eyes, dark urine, severe tummy pain or new neurological symptoms urgently.
risks: Bleeding, blood clots and high blood pressure
Kidney injury or protein in urine
Rare bowel perforation, ischaemic colitis or PRES

phases.label: Tablet-only continuation
phases.detail: Twice daily every day;28-day review cycles while helping and tolerable. No fixed total number of cycles.

timeline.label: Nintedanib twice daily
timeline.text: Continuous every day; no scheduled week off.

timeline.label: Safety and benefit review
timeline.text: Keep the agreed monthly / cycle tests.

day_groups.title: Nintedanib every day
day_groups.body: Take your prescribed capsule dose twice daily about 12 hours apart, including Day 1. There is no docetaxel in this phase.
day_groups.action: Use the current prescription and contact plan.

support.title: Capsules
support.text: Take nintedanib about 12 hours apart with food; swallow whole. Do not open, chew or crush. If missed, take the next scheduled dose only; never double up.

support.title: Diarrhoea plan
support.text: Have the prescribed anti-diarrhoeal and fluid plan ready. Contact oncology early for diarrhoea, poor intake or vomiting; do not wait 7 days to seek help.

support.title: Medicine review
support.text: Check all medicines and supplements with oncology/pharmacy. Nintedanib has P-gp interactions; docetaxel has CYP 3 A interactions, including grapefruit concerns.

support.title: Pregnancy prevention
support.text: Discuss fertility and effective contraception. Nintedanib requires contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after; follow the longest advice for your complete regimen. Vomiting/diarrhoea can reduce pill absorption.

questions.a: Your treating team checks the prescription, tests and symptoms. A completed-cycle stamp records past treatment; it does not authorise the next dose.
Ask the team to update your phase, medicines, test appointments and cycle record. Use the updated prescription.
Your team sets a response and follow-up plan for your cancer and symptoms. This document does not invent a fixed scan or tumour-marker timetable.

sources.title: NCCP antiemetic classification v 6 and oral pathway

indication_text: NCCP 00372 a: locally advanced, metastatic stageIIIB/IV or locally recurrent adenocarcinoma NSCLC after first-line chemotherapy.
schedule_summary: Take the prescribed nintedanib dose twice daily every day. Reviews are organised in 28-day cycles; there is no planned tablet-free week. This phase starts only after at least 4 combination cycles and team approval.
administration_text: Nintedanib starting dose 200 mg per dose twice daily about 12 hours apart, preferably with food, continuously including Day 1 of each 28-day cycle. Confirm any reduced prescribed dose. Docetaxel is no longer included; do not carry its Day 1 omission into this phase.
monitoring_summary: Phase and recovery review: At least 4 completed combination cycles and consultant approval; confirm new capsule plan. Blood count, kidney and liver tests: Before each 28-day cycle; liver tests at least monthly, more often if needed. Blood pressure, symptoms and medicines: BP periodically/as indicated; extra tests for liver-risk factors or symptoms. Response, scans and recovery: Agree response and follow-up timing; no fixed scan or tumour-marker interval.
urgent_extra: Call your oncology team immediately for fever, shaking chills, sudden illness, breathing difficulty, chest pain, significant bleeding, severe tummy pain, uncontrolled vomiting or new severe headache, confusion, seizure or vision change. Do not wait for the next appointment.
consent_support: Discuss the goal, alternatives, important risks for you, fertility/pregnancy prevention, practical support and what would prompt changing or stopping treatment.

chronology_notes.title: Symptoms can occur at any time
chronology_notes.text: Side effects and infection do not follow a guaranteed day-by-day risk curve. Contact the team when symptoms occur.

chronology_notes.title: Changes for safety
chronology_notes.text: Treatment may be delayed, reduced or stopped. Do not make up missed doses or change your tablets yourself.

timeline_note: Relative days without personal dates. The team confirms actual treatment and test dates.
safety_note: Call your oncology team immediately for fever, shaking chills, sudden illness, breathing difficulty, chest pain, significant bleeding, severe tummy pain, uncontrolled vomiting or new severe headache, confusion, seizure or vision change. Do not wait for the next appointment.
passport_visit_note: Record the actual phase, dose dates, symptoms and interruptions. A completed-cycle stamp is a record of treatment, not clearance for another dose.
anatomy: New severe headache, confusion, seizure or visual change needs urgent advice.
Chest pain, sudden breathlessness or a swollen painful leg needs urgent assessment.
Attend monthly liver tests; report yellow skin/eyes or dark urine.
Call early for diarrhoea or vomiting; severe abdominal pain is urgent.
Report swelling, foamy urine or much less urine.
Report bleeding or poor wound healing. Tell oncology before procedures.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: The trial found a progression-free benefit overall and an overall-survival benefit in the prespecified adenocarcinoma subgroup.
evidence.interpretation: The licensed/NCCP population is adenocarcinoma after first-line chemotherapy. Overall-population PFS and adenocarcinoma-subgroup OS are labelled separately; this does not establish an independent benefit from maintenance-only initiation.
